subject: Private deployment: Crestline VPC peering & on-prem agent planning
messages:
From: Simon Wu <simon.wu@crestline-analytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@crestline-analytics.com>; laura.bennett@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: Crestline VPC peering & on-prem agent planning

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the kick-off call earlier. As promised I'm sending our current networking constraints and a couple of questions so we can lock the cutover window. High level: we plan to run Redwood Private inside our primary us-west-2 VPC and a small on-prem ingestion appliance in our Vancouver datacenter for low-latency ingest.

Items for Redwood team:
- Confirm VPC peering vs Transit Gateway recommendation for a single-account setup (Crestline prefers peering if performance overhead is negligible).
- IP space: we'll allocate 10.40.0.0/16 for Crestline service VPC and leave 10.41.0.0/24 reserved for the appliance. Please confirm there are no conflicts on Redwood side.
- Private endpoints: we need a list of service FQDNs and port requirements (eg. 443, 8443 for agent control plane).
- On-prem agent: installer should run on CentOS 8 and we need an offline package option. Can you provide the installer SHA256 and expected disk/memory requirements?

Attachments: network diagram (draft), endpoint matrix, and our local firewall rules.

Target timeline: plan to start configuration the week of Mar 20 and do a staged cutover Mar 28 (non-prod) -> Apr 4 (prod). Let us know if that fits Redwood's ops calendar.

—Simon
Simon Wu
Director, Infrastructure
Crestline Analytics
---
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Wu <simon.wu@crestline-analytics.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: Crestline VPC peering & on-prem agent planning

Thanks Simon — helpful notes. Looping in Laura (Network PM) and Marissa (Implementation CS lead) and Karthik (Networking SME) to confirm action items below.

Quick answers and next steps:
1) VPC peering vs TGW: Karthik recommends simple VPC peering for your single-account design — lower ops complexity and better hop latency. We'll provide a peering acceptance checklist and sample route-map. If you expect to expand to multi-account or multi-region later we'll revisit TGW.

2) IP ranges: 10.40.0.0/16 and 10.41.0.0/24 look fine from our side; no overlap with Redwood sample ranges. We'll include a CIDR validation step in the preflight.

3) Private endpoints & ports: see attached endpoint matrix (private-endpoints-matrix.xlsx). Primary ports: 443 (control plane), 8443 (agent), 22 (optional for support jumpbox, restrict by source IP). TLS required on all endpoints; mTLS optional depending on your cert policies.

4) On-prem installer: we'll provide an offline tarball and an installer script. Minimum agent footprint: 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 50 GB disk. Offline package will include checksums and install verification steps. Marissa will share the package and checklist.

Action items:
- Marissa: prepare on-prem installer tarball + checklist and share GDrive link by Tue Mar 7.
- Karthik: produce peering checklist and sample route tables by Mon Mar 6.
- Laura: block a 2-hour preflight review with Crestline for Mar 15 (networking + security review).

Simon — can you confirm if you need HSM/KMS integration now or deferred to a later phase? Also please share the list of support engineers who should be allowed SSH access to the jumpbox (if enabled).

Regards,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 07 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: Crestline VPC peering & on-prem agent planning

Hi Simon — attaching the installer checklist and a first-pass offline package manifest (onprem-installer-checklist.txt). Highlights:
- Offline tarball (redwood-agent-offline-1.3.0.tar.gz) will include prebuilt binaries for CentOS 7/8 and Ubuntu 20.04, install.sh, systemd unit, and a post-install health check.
- Agent resource profile: 4 vCPU / 8GB RAM / 50GB disk as Irene mentioned.
- Upgrade path: we support in-place upgrades with a safe rollback flag.
- SHA256: d2f7b0a7c8b9f3e4f8c8a6d7a2c5b6e3f9a1bdc4a3f2e6d7b8c9a0e1f2d3c4b5

Schedule note: I can share the package link and install instructions by EOD Tue Mar 7. For the staged cutover dates (Mar 28 non-prod, Apr 4 prod) I suggest we run a dry-install on a lab VM on Mar 22 to exercise the offline path. Will that fit your schedule?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: crestline-network-diagram-v1.pdf; private-endpoints-matrix.xlsx; onprem-installer-checklist.txt

- HSM/KMS integration: deferred to phase 2 (we'll use our cloud KMS today).
- SSH jumpbox: enable restricted access for the following users: a.kapoor@crestline-analytics.com, s.lee@crestline-analytics.com (source IPs will be shared in the preflight).

- Please use the HubSpot record https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/companies/CRS-2028-0142 for checklist sign-offs; we'll route approvals through that pipeline.

Best,
Simon
